'''Troy Alan Carter''' (born July 31, 1973)<ref>{{Cite web|last=Congress|first=The Library of|title=LC Linked Data Service: Authorities and Vocabularies (Library of Congress)|url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/no2001075646.html|access-date=2020-11-30|website=id.loc.gov}}</ref> is an American plasma [[physicist]] and the Director of Fusion Energy Division at Oak Ridge National Laboratory.  He was formerly a professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Troy Carter|url=http://www.physics.ucla.edu/~tcarter/|access-date=2020-07-24|website=www.physics.ucla.edu}}</ref> He was co-awarded the 2002 [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research]] for his work on driven [[magnetic reconnection]] in a laboratory plasma.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=2002 John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research Recipient|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Carter&first_nm=Troy&year=2002|access-date=2020-07-24|website=American Physical Society|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ji|first1=Hantao|last2=Carter|first2=Troy|last3=Hsu|first3=Scott|last4=Yamada|first4=Masaaki|date=2001|title=Study of local reconnection physics in a laboratory plasma|journal=Earth, Planets and Space|language=en|volume=53|issue=6|pages=539–545|doi=10.1186/BF03353267|bibcode=2001EP&S...53..539J|issn=1880-5981|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Carter received a [[Bachelor of Science]] (B.S.) in physics and a B.S. in [[nuclear engineering]] from [[North Carolina State University]] in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://science.osti.gov/-/media/fes/fesac/pdf/2019/2019-2022_Membership_Bios.pdf?la=en&hash=265EBB17C0710184C915297846E4E6E7285A0E9E |title=BIOGRAPHIES OF FESAC MEMBERS |access-date=July 25, 2020 |archive-date=July 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200725031135/https://science.osti.gov/-/media/fes/fesac/pdf/2019/2019-2022_Membership_Bios.pdf?la=en&hash=265EBB17C0710184C915297846E4E6E7285A0E9E |url-status=dead }}</ref> He then received a [[Master of Arts]] and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in Astrophysical Sciences from [[Princeton University]] in 1997 and 2001 respectively, where he was supervised by [[Masaaki Yamada]] and [[Russell Kulsrud]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Graduate Theses {{!}} Princeton Program in Plasma Physics|url=https://plasma.princeton.edu/education/graduate-theses|access-date=2020-07-24|website=plasma.princeton.edu}}</ref><ref>Carter, Troy Alan (2001) [http://www.physics.ucla.edu/~tcarter/publications/tac_thesis.pdf Experimental Studies of Fluctuations In a Reconnecting Current Sheet], Ph.D. Thesis</ref> Upon graduation, Carter was awarded a Fusion Energy Postdoctoral Fellowship from the [[United States Department of Energy|US Department of Energy]] and pursued his postdoctoral work at UCLA.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Taming turbulence in plasmas: from magnetic fusion energy to black hole accretion disks, Dr. Troy Carter, Dept. of Physics & Astronomy, UCLA|url=https://calendar.clemson.edu/event/taming_turbulence_in_plasmas_from_magnetic_fusion_energy_to_black_hole_accretion_disks_dr_troy_carter_dept_of_physics_astronomy_ucla|access-date=2020-07-25|website=Clemson University|language=en}}</ref>

In 2002, Carter became a faculty member at UCLA's department of physics and astronomy. He was an [[assistant professor|Assistant Professor]] until 2008 where he was promoted to [[associate professor|Associate Professor]], and was later promoted to full [[Professor]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Carter |first1=Davis |title=Short Resume |url=http://www.physics.ucla.edu/~tcarter/bio_short_parbox.pdf |access-date=22 March 2022}}</ref> In 2016, he became the director of the [[Basic Plasma Science Facility]] and oversaw the renewal of the facility funding from the Department of Energy and the [[National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=NSF Award Search: Award#1561912 - Basic Plasma Science Facility Renewal|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1561912|access-date=2020-07-24|website=www.nsf.gov}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-09-22|title=Troy Carter|url=https://www.ioes.ucla.edu/person/troy-carter/|access-date=2020-07-24|website=Institute of the Environment and Sustainability at UCLA|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2017, he became a director of the Plasma Science and Technology Institute at UCLA.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.nap.edu/read/25802/chapter/14|title=Plasma Science: Enabling Technology, Sustainability, Security, and Exploration|publisher=The National Academies Press|year=2021|language=en|chapter=Appendix D: Committee Member Biographical Information|doi=10.17226/25802|isbn=978-0-309-67760-8|s2cid=219808013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Plasma Science and Technology Institute {{!}} UCLA Physics & Astronomy|url=http://psti.ucla.edu/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200423104424/http://psti.ucla.edu/|archive-date=2020-04-23|access-date=2020-07-25|website=psti.ucla.edu}}</ref>  Carter led the DOE Fusion Energy Sciences Advisory Committee (FESAC) Subcommittee on Long Range Planning in 2020, resulting in the report "Powering the Future: Fusion and Plasmas"<ref>{{Cite web |title=Powering the Future Fusion & Plasmas |url=https://usfusionandplasmas.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241218004552/https://usfusionandplasmas.org/ |archive-date=2024-12-18 |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=usfusionandplasmas.org |language=en}}</ref> published in 2021.  In 2024, Carter assumed the role of Director of Fusion Energy Division<ref>{{Cite web |last=Energy |first=UT-Battelle LLC for the US Department of |date=2024-07-11 |title=Carter to lead Fusion Energy Division at Oak Ridge National Laboratory |url=https://www.ornl.gov/news/carter-lead-fusion-energy-division-oak-ridge-national-laboratory-0 |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=www.ornl.gov |language=en}}</ref> at Oak Ridge National Laboratory.  

== Honors and awards ==
In 2002, Carter was jointly awarded the [[John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research]] with Hantao Ji, [[Masaaki Yamada]] and Scott Hsu for "''the experimental investigation of driven magnetic reconnection in a laboratory plasma. In this work, careful diagnostic studies of the current sheet structure, dynamics and associated wave activity provide a comprehensive picture of the reconnection process.''"<ref name=":0" />   In 2014, Carter was inducted as a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], with citation "For novel and impactful experimental research into fundamental processes relevant to laboratory, space and astrophysical plasmas including magnetic reconnection, wave-wave interactions, and turbulence and transport in magnetically-confined plasmas."<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2014&unit_id=DPP&institution=University+of+California%2C+Los+Angeles|access-date=2020-07-24|website=American Physical Society|language=en}}</ref>  In 2021, Carter was selected for the Fusion Power Associates Leadership award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FPA Awards |url=https://fusionpower.org/Awards.html |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=fusionpower.org}}</ref>
